newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds close higher after long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds close higher after long weekend.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher across the board on Tuesday following the long Independence Day weekend, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.10 to 105.10
Volume including Makams was 160 million shekels, which Miri Dagan, a trader at Clal Insurance, described as average.
"There was demand in all the segments: index-linked, Kfirs and others," said Dagan.
CPI-linked bonds resumed their rising trend of last week against a background of buoyant demand and tighter supply, which Dagan said was due to fewer government issues this month.
Dagan noted that CPI-linked yields were now at 4.15-4.2 percent, putting them at the lower end of their range of 4.1-4.3 percent since the start of the year.
In the unlinked segment, yields on the Makam reached 13.95 percent. "There wasn't any trading for a few days ... so prices naturally rise," said Hoffman.
"I think that all told the trend will be mixed. There won't be any lowering of interest rates," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments and Securities.
Israel's base rate is 13.9 percent, where it has been since the end of February. The Bank of Israel will announce any change at the end of May.

The market is expecting a high April consumer price index of about 1.3 percent and looking for the full-year inflation rate to be about 10 percent, Hoffman said. The April CPI will be published on Thursday.

Dollar-linked bonds were higher in response to the dollar's strengthening against the shekel. The shekel representative rate against the U.S. currency was 3.4010 compared with 3.3990 on Friday in the local foreign currency market. "Basically there was little change in trading," Dagan said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
